scams.name: Dive Shop Open Water Pricing & Quality Manipulation
scams.description: You walk into a Sairee Beach dive shop and see ‘PADI Open Water Course — 9,500 baht!’ on the sidewalk sign. At checkout, the add-ons start: 500 baht for the textbook, 300 for the mask rental, 400 for certification-card processing, 200 per boat day fee — 11,500 baht and climbing. r/ThailandTourism ‘What is the price for scuba diving in Koh Tao?’ sets the benchmark: ‘Open Water course, 10,000 baht give or take a couple thousand. DSD around 3,000–4,000.’ So 9,500-baht sidewalk prices hiding 11,500-baht real totals is not a 30 percent markup — it’s opaque pricing designed to pull you through the door.
scams.avoidance: Budget 11,500–12,500 baht total for Open Water certification; anything significantly under either hides fees or cuts safety. Book with verified long-term shops: Black Turtle Dive, Big Blue Diving, Koh Tao Divers, Crystal Dive. Get a written breakdown of every cost before paying — textbook, mask rental, cert card, boat fees. Insist on confined-water skill practice before open-water dives. Check the shop’s Google and r/scubadiving reviews for 2024–2025 safety incidents before booking.
scams.location: Sairee Beach dive shops, Mae Haad pier dive shops, Chalok Baan Kao

scams.name: Beach Entrance Fees & Private-Beach Gate Keepers
scams.description: You scooter to Freedom Beach on the southwest coast of Koh Tao. At the access path, a gate and a man in a chair demand 100 baht per person, ‘beach entrance fee.’ In Thailand, all beaches are legally public up to the high-tide line — so access charges are structurally semi-legal at best, yet they’re widespread on Koh Tao. r/ThailandTourism ‘This is why tourists have trust issues’ captures the frustration: ‘Almost every beach on Koh Tao charges a fee to enter, and the beaches are littered with trash. With all the money made from entrances, you’d think they could clean up.’ r/ThailandTourism ‘Koh Tao — free beaches for snorkeling?’ answers the obvious question plainly: ‘It’s a scam.’
scams.avoidance: Thai beaches are legally public up to the high-tide line, so ‘beach fees’ are semi-legal at best. Focus on verifiably free beaches: Sairee Beach main strip, public Mae Haad, and the public sections of Chalok Baan Kao. If charged, ask for a printed receipt with a business name; real fees produce documentation. Budget 50–200 baht per beach for paid-access spots only if you specifically want Freedom Beach or Aow Leuk. Report persistent demands at truly public beaches to Tourist Police on 1155.
scams.location: Freedom Beach, Shark Bay, Aow Leuk, Tanote Bay, Hin Ngam Bay access

scams.name: Scooter Rental Passport-Hostage Damage (฿20K Variant)
scams.description: You rent a scooter on Sairee for 200 baht a day. Koh Tao’s hilly roads and unpaved paths are notorious — r/ThailandTourism ‘Crashed scooter, paid in cash. Should I just leave it?’ describes it: ‘First time riding the scooter and did a good amount of damage when I crashed into a wall. Paid 3,000 for the deposit.’ The 3,000-baht deposit is the standard Koh Tao rate, but the damage quote is separate and highly variable. r/ThailandTourism ‘Scratched the bike, what’s the honest price?’ captures the long-standing hostage quote: a scooter dent in Samui or Tao, and the shop demands 20,000 baht on the spot or no passport back.
scams.avoidance: Consider not renting a scooter on Koh Tao. The roads are genuinely dangerous, and multiple tourist deaths are documented. If you do rent, never leave your original passport; offer a 5,000–10,000 baht cash deposit and walk if refused. Photograph every panel including the underside, timestamped. Rent from long-term shops with 200+ Google reviews (Mr. J Rentals Sairee is one) rather than pier storefronts. If hit with a fake damage quote, take the community-recommended exit: leave a small cash deposit, retrieve your passport, and park the scooter back at the shop overnight.
scams.location: Sairee Beach rental shops, Mae Haad pier rentals, Chalok Baan Kao scooter shops

scams.name: Tour No-Show Deposit Blackmail & ‘Sorry, Cancelled’ Fee
scams.description: You book a Koh Nang Yuan snorkeling day trip at a Sairee booking booth for 1,200 baht. They take your deposit in cash, no receipt. The next morning you oversleep and miss the pickup by 20 minutes. You go to reschedule; the shop claims the boat has already left and demands another 1,200 baht to rebook. r/ThailandTourism ‘Being threatened by the police for missing a snorkelling’ documents the scenario: the tour company threatened police involvement after the tourist missed their booking. Community consensus was mixed — some read it as a no-show fee, others as an aggressive enforcement tactic.
scams.avoidance: Book tours on Klook or 12go.asia with a free-cancellation window where possible. Confirm the actual boat or operator name in writing, not just the booth’s brand. Pay by credit card for chargeback leverage on no-show disputes. Know the Sail Rock benchmark: 2,500–3,000 baht including two dives. Anything higher is a booth markup. Verify the boat operator’s recent safety record on r/scubadiving or Google before booking.
scams.location: Sairee Beach tour booking booths, Mae Haad pier tour desks, hotel-lobby tour sales

scams.name: ‘Murder Island’ Family-Mafia Extortion (Rare But Real)
scams.description: Koh Tao carries a dark reputation most Thai islands don’t. The nickname ‘Murder Island’ emerged from a decade of unexplained tourist deaths — Irish backpacker David Miller and Briton Hannah Witheridge (2014), Belgian Elise Dallemagne (2017), Swiss tourist Nicole Sauvain-Weisskopf (2018), a Russian tourist in 2020, and multiple 2024–2025 cases including a November 2025 sexual assault attempt on a Canadian tourist reported by *Khaosod English*. r/Thailand ‘Families of murdered tourists on Koh Tao, dubbed Death Island’ captures the local view: ‘Everyone knows mafia runs those southern islands and the cops are on the take. Keep to yourself, don’t stick your nose into anything.’
scams.avoidance: Travel with a buddy and share your live location with at least one person at home. Stay on the Sairee Beach main strip after dark; avoid isolated beaches at night. Do not accept drinks, pills, or shroom shakes from strangers under any circumstance. If a dispute with a local business escalates to threats, leave the island on the next ferry — do not try to win it. Save Tourist Police 1155 and your embassy’s emergency line in your phone before you arrive.
scams.location: Koh Tao island-wide — particularly beach-adjacent incidents off-hours
